cycles.rationale: The sphere has a large negative yaw error with zero drift and stable contact, so I start an early coarse thumb-biased rotation rather than holding or finishing.
Large yaw error (-66 deg) with action_05 having worsened full-orientation error, so switch to an untried coarse-rotation primitive from a different contact group to seek positive yaw gain.

Both coarse rotations increased rot_dist_rad and tilt while drift_xy doubled to 0.0246 (>=0.02) with rotation stalled, so I will recenter/reseat the grasp before attempting further orientation correction.

action_15 is the only tried primitive with positive gains in yaw (+2.766 deg toward the needed positive correction), rot_dist (+0.0747 rad), tilt (+7.093 deg), and position, so continuing it is best while error remains large.
With low drift but large negative Y tilt and yaw error on a sphere, probe the dedicated sphere Y-orientation primitive while preserving stable contact.
The sphere still has large negative Y and Z error with low drift, and action_19 worsened full orientation/Y error, so I’ll try the opposed sphere-Y thumb sweep to correct the dominant Y component.

Drift is stable and the dominant error is large negative Y with negative Z; tried sphere-Y sweeps action_19/action_20 gave positive Y gain that worsened the negative Y error, so I’m probing the untried reverse thumb-cycle action_21 for opposite-sign Y correction.

Drift is low (0.0138 m) so the reseat advisory is not triggered; with dominant Z error (-49.8 deg needing positive yaw) and rot_dist 1.125 rad, action_15 is the only primitive with consistent positive yaw (+5 to +7 deg) and two helpful uses with the best mean rot_dist gain (0.0622 rad), so I repeat it while its gain remains above stall.

The sphere still has large full-orientation error dominated by negative Y tilt, and action_21 previously gave the best rot_dist and tilt reduction while improving the negative Y component, with drift remaining low.

action_21 has produced the best full-orientation gains (+0.0826 and +0.0606 rad) and the largest tilt reductions on this sphere, is only at two uses with no decay, and angular velocity is low so no hold is needed.

action_21 has consistently reduced full-orientation error (rot_dist gains ~0.06-0.08 rad per use) and its latest XYZ gains match the signs of all current error components, with only 2 consecutive uses and no stall, so continuing it is the best path while spin is low and drift is safe.

action_21 has stalled after three consecutive uses (last rot_dist gain 0.0025 < 0.01), while the large negative Y component (-39.9 deg) dominates tilt, so switch to an untried three-axis/contact-escape probe targeting Y rather than repeat the decayed thumb cycle.

With low spin and negligible drift, action_21 has stalled and action_17 just worsened full-orientation error, so I’m switching to an untried different-contact three-axis probe to attack the dominant negative-Y/tilt error while preserving positive yaw progress.
The sphere is stable with low drift but has a large Y/tilt error, so I’ll try the untried three-axis probe action_16 rather than repeating stalled thumb-cycle actions.
Grasp is stable and action_16 just produced positive yaw with a full-orientation gain, so continue that three-axis probe rather than switching while rot_dist is still improving.

The dominant error is the Y component (-53.5 deg) on a sphere, and action_20 is a sphere Y-orientation probe that previously produced a +6.9 deg Y gain with a positive rot_dist gain (+0.0077) and only one use, so repeating it should keep reducing the full orientation error.

With low drift, moderate spin, and dominant negative Y/negative Z error, action_16 has the best recent full-orientation gains and its last XYZ gains matched the needed Y/Z correction without destabilizing the grasp.

Tilt is still large (~52 deg, dominated by -51.9 deg Y) and action_16 just gave the best full-orientation gain (+0.0702 rad) with all XYZ components moving in the useful sign and minimal drift, so I continue it rather than switching to the negative-gain or stalled Y-probes.
The sphere is stable with tiny drift and action_16 is still giving consistent full-orientation and tilt gains, so continue it rather than switching to a mixed Y-probe.

The dominant Y/tilt error (~-47 deg) is being steadily reduced by action_16 with positive rot_dist gains (~0.045 rad, well above the 0.01 decay threshold) and correct-sign Y gains, while drift is minimal and the Y-probe alternatives (19/20) worsened rot_dist and 21 has stalled, so continuing the productive primitive is best.
action_16 is still reducing the dominant negative Y tilt and full orientation error with stable drift, so I will continue it rather than switch while gains remain strong.

The dominant error is Y=-42.5 deg with rot_dist still 0.79 rad, and action_16 is the only primitive reliably reducing full orientation error every cycle (last rot_dist gain +0.0439 rad, Y gain -2.2 deg matching the negative Y-error sign) with near-zero drift and no stall (gain well above 0.01), so continuing it is the highest-EV steady correction.
action_16 is still reducing rot_dist_rad, yaw error, and the dominant negative Y tilt with stable drift, so continue it rather than switching while gains remain strong.

action_16 is still strongly reducing full-orientation error (last rot_dist gain +0.0738 rad, recent mean +0.059, positive trend) with correct-sign gains on all XYZ components and minimal drift, whereas the sphere-Y probes (19/20) previously worsened rot_dist, so I continue the working primitive.
action_16 has consistently reduced all error components for 8 straight cycles with latest rot_dist gain of +0.0799 rad and tilt gain of +4.45 deg, and drift is minimal so it should be continued.

action_16 continues to deliver strong consistent gains (last rot_dist gain 0.076 rad, tilt reduced ~4 deg per cycle) against the dominant -27.9 deg Y error, with negligible drift and no sign of stalling, so continuing it is best.
rot_dist_rad is still high and dominated by Y tilt, while action_16 is steadily reducing tilt and full-orientation error without drift or stall.

Success is false with rot_dist_rad still 0.3675 and tilt dominated by Y error, while action_16 remains stable and still produces positive full-orientation and tilt gains, so continue it rather than switching or holding.

Yaw is nearly zero but rot_dist 0.37 rad is driven by a dominant negative Y tilt (-17.9 deg); action_16 has stalled after 12 straight uses (last rot_dist gain negative), so I switch to the sphere Y-orientation probe action_21, whose historical Y and tilt gains have the right sign and whose mean rot_dist gain is positive, and spin (0.15 rad/s) is moderate enough not to require a hold.

With action_16 stalled and action_21 just worsening full-orientation error, the still-large X/Y tilt (26.7 deg) calls for an untried alternate-contact primitive to change the contact pattern while drift remains low and stable.

Residual error is dominated by X/Y tilt (16.7 deg, rot_dist 0.295) with low spin and stable grasp, and action_04 just delivered the largest rot_dist (0.172 rad) and tilt (~10 deg) gains after only one use, so continue it while avoiding stalled action_16 and harmful action_21.

The dominant error is the negative X tilt (-15.5 deg, tilt 16.5) with all XYZ errors negative and a stable low-drift grasp; action_04 (just stalled on 2 consecutive uses) and action_16 (overused, now worsens X) are avoided, while action_20 is a different under-used thumb contact group whose measured gains are negative for X and Z (matching the negative errors) with near-neutral full-orientation cost.

With drift stable and the dominant error a negative X/tilt component, action_04 previously gave the largest rot_dist and tilt reduction with negative X/Y gains, and it is not being repeated consecutively after action_20.

action_04 is the only primitive consistently reducing rot_dist (latest +0.0429 rad), tilt (+2.8 deg), and the dominant negative X error while drift stays low, and its latest gain is still above the 0.01 rad decay threshold so continuing is warranted.

Tilt error remains large (X=-16.74 dominant) while the recent X/Y probes (16/20/21) and thumb cycles show stalled or decaying rot_dist gains, and action_04 has hit its two-consecutive-use limit, so I switch to an untried multi-finger contact-refresh to reset the contact pattern before resuming orientation correction.
Residual sphere spin is moderately high while drift is stable, so a brief zero-command hold should damp motion before the next X/tilt correction.

Yaw is near zero but rot_dist is large (0.390) dominated by X=-22.2 deg and tilt 22.4 deg; action_04 is the only recent primitive with positive rot_dist and tilt gains plus a negative X-axis gain matching the negative X error, and it is not in a stalled consecutive run.

The dominant error is the X component (-22.416 deg, tilt 22.4) while yaw is only ~6 deg; action_15 has by far the strongest measured X gain of matching negative sign (-13.976) with positive mean rot_dist and position gains, and it has not been used recently.

The dominant errors are X (-17.9 deg) and Y (+18.0 deg), and action_17 is the only tried probe whose measured gains match both signs (X -8.3, Y +11.6 deg), directly attacking the 25.4 deg tilt on this sphere.

Tilt (22.7 deg) and Y error dominate rot_dist, and action_17 was the best recent performer (rot_dist +0.034 rad, tilt +2.67 deg, Y +8.25 deg) with only 2 uses and no stall, so I continue it to keep reducing full-orientation error.

Tilt (X/Y) still dominates at 19.19 deg with X=-17.357 the largest component, and the last two action_17 runs reduced rot_dist (0.452->0.389) and tilt with gains still above 0.01 rad, while drift and spin are low and stable, so I continue it to keep cutting full-orientation error before addressing the growing yaw.

action_17 has been repeated three times and its latest run increased rot_dist_rad and yaw error (stalled/decayed), while drift and spin are low, so I switch to an untried multi-finger contact-refresh (action_07) to re-form a stable contact pattern before resuming X/Y orientation correction.

Drift is tiny and stable but rot_dist_rad=0.5565 with a dominant X/tilt error (~26 deg) after action_07 destabilized the sphere, so I switch to the most reliable three-axis orientation probe (14/14 helpful, best mean rot_dist gain) to attack the large X/Y error.

The dominant error is the X tilt component (-23 deg) and action_16 just reduced both tilt and full geodesic distance (last gain +0.051 rad, tilt gain +1.83 deg) with low drift and low spin, so continuing this proven three-axis probe is the best option.

action_16 is heavily used and stalled (latest rot_dist gain -0.0141 < 0.01), so per guidance I switch to an untried contact-escape in a different finger group (little finger) to refresh contacts while drift is low and the dominant X/tilt error persists.

The dominant error is the -21.7 deg X component with 27 deg tilt, recent probes (16/17/13/07) stalled or worsened rot_dist, and action_18 is a little-used three-axis probe whose single use gave positive X gain (+4.45 deg) and a net positive full-orientation gain (+0.029 rad), so it is the best contact-group change to attack the X/Y tilt.
Drift is low but rot_dist and tilt remain large while action_16 has decayed, so I’m switching to an untried wrist-based coarse rotation to change contact and attack the X/Y error.

Tilt/X-Y error dominates (tilt 30.2 deg, Y +22.7, X -19.9) while yaw is modest; action_18 is a three-axis probe whose last use gave correctly-signed X/Y/Z gains and positive rot_dist (+0.0186) and tilt (+1.168) gains, and it is not stalled or overused.

The dominant error is now positive Z/yaw (+23.2 deg) needing negative yaw, and action_06 is the only tried primitive with measured negative yaw (-7.242 deg) and positive Z-axis gain (+7.18 deg); drift (0.0105 m) and spin (0.286 rad/s) are still stable enough for a coarse rotation rather than a hold.

The dominant remaining error is three-axis tilt (X=-17.5, Y=+17.7, rot_dist=0.550) with stable drift, and action_16 has the best episode record for full-orientation gain and the desired mean X-positive/Y-negative correction pattern.
